qualification: Local loopback measurements with bounded async writes, two order-balanced repeats per unprofiled phase. Host was available overnight; no statistical significance or general workload ranking is claimed. Profiles are diagnostic and kept separate from speed comparisons.

decisions.description: Combine up to four ready TLS records in one owner-shared 66 KiB output buffer.
Two DATA frames in one transport borrow saved some CPU but worsened same-connection foreground p99; all production changes restored.

decisions.decision: Refined to remove tiny remainder records
decisions.description: At most eight wraps and 128 KiB plaintext in one shared 130 KiB ciphertext buffer per owner. Same maximum 131216-byte plaintext allowance; ordinary buffer fallback when shared lease occupied. This intermediate variant still emits tiny remainder records.
After acknowledging a large TLS batch, yield the owner visit instead of wrapping a tiny remainder of the byte allowance. Same maximum work bound; fewer records, writes and sampled allocation.

The extra remaining-allowance condition did not show a consistent benefit. Java 21 median p99 fell about 5.7% with overlapping ranges, but Java 25 p99 rose about 7.7% and CPU rose about 1.4%. The longer original-versus-selected control did not reproduce the earlier short-run 64 KiB latency penalty, so the added condition is not justified.
decisions.validation: 175 focused Java 21 tests passed; eight fixed-rate trials passed; isolated source never copied into production.
